messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p95 latency SLO tripped for routing policy 'smart-latency-v2' in us-west-2. Detected repeated reroutes between us-west-2 and us-east-1 + fallback to low-qual model-quantized-v1 over the last 6m. Oscillation count=7. Autoscale did not resolve. Paging lucas (oncall).
Lucas (oncall): I'm on it. Paging PD and grabbing context. Who owns the routing policy? @Sanjay?
Sanjay (infra): Yep, that policy rollout was part of the latency rollouts from last night. I pushed an aggressive weight shift to favor lower-cost regions at 01:12 UTC. Seeing the alert now.
Maria (sre): Adding telemetry: p95 jumped from ~220ms normal to 980ms at 21:07 UTC, then routing triggered fallback to model-quantized-v1 which reduced latency to 320ms but increased error/degeneration complaints. Then traffic bounced back to primary region causing repeated re-evaluations.
Ophelia (product): We're getting CS reports that a handful of customers saw hallucination/regression after fallback — which customers are impacted? EMMA from CS is in thread.
CS Ops (emma): We have two active enterprise sessions (accts: fastchat-inc, neo-search) that reported degraded output. I'll start a customer notice once we confirm mitigation.
Lucas (oncall): Immediate plan: 1) Pause smart routing weight adjustments, 2) Pin routing to stable variant for affected routes, 3) Disable cross-region fallback for the moment, 4) Roll back the 'aggressive-latency-v2' policy. I'll do 1-3 now.
Sanjay (infra): Acknowledged. Command to pin routes (prod):
```
redwoodctl route set --route /v1/generate --policy smart-latency-v1 --force --reason "incident 1958123456 pin to stable"
```
Applying now.
deploy-bot: deploy started: route-change-1958123456 by sanjay at 21:12:36 UTC
Lucas (oncall): Also setting the policy cooldown to avoid immediate re-eval (temporarily raise window to 120s):
```
redwoodctl config set routing.smart_eval_window 120
```
Maria (sre): Watching metrics. Query I ran to find top impacted customers (by session count + degraded model fallback):
```
SELECT customer_id, count(*) as fallbacks
FROM routing_logs
WHERE timestamp > now() - interval '15 minutes' AND fallback_model = 'model-quantized-v1'
GROUP BY customer_id
ORDER BY fallbacks DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
Results: fastchat-inc (42), neo-search (18), alpha-saas (6).
CS Ops (emma): Noted. I'll prepare a short incident notice for fastchat-inc and neo-search. No public status page update yet until we confirm resolution.
Maria (sre): Observability note: the decision engine is using short-term p95 windows (30s) for re-routing. That high sensitivity + asymmetric cold cache latencies in us-west-2 is causing flip/flop. We should increase smoothing and add hysteresis.
Sanjay (infra): I rolled back the 'aggressive-latency-v2' weight push and set a staged canary instead.
deploy-bot: rollback completed: policy-rollout-2026-06-12T01:12 reverted by sanjay
Lucas (oncall): After pin + rollback: p95 in affected routes dropped to ~300ms, reroute count fell to 1 in last 5m. Customers still seeing degraded quality? @emma
CS Ops (emma): fastchat-inc confirms output looks back to normal on their side. neo-search sees improvement but still intermittent for a single session.
Ophelia (product): We need to track the quality regression from fallback model-quantized-v1; create an eval for the affected prompt set and tie to rollout gates.
Maria (sre): Action item for infra/release: change re-eval window from 30s -> 90s and add minimum stable duration for any route change to 120s. Also add an oscillation detector to auto-suppress repeated reroutes when count > 3 in 10m.
Sanjay (infra): Agreed. I'll open the PR and target hotfix today. Patch plan:
- Increase smoothing: routing.smart_eval_window=90
- Add min_route_stable_seconds=120
- Oscillation cutoff: if reroute_count > 3 then mark route as 'cooldown' for 10m.
Lucas (oncall): For the incident timeline and paging: I accepted page at 21:11 UTC, mitigation (pin + rollback) completed by 21:16 UTC, observed stabilized metrics by 21:20 UTC. I'm moving to mitigation monitoring (watching for 30m). If it stays stable, we'll close.
Maria (sre): Observability logs excerpt (correlation):
```
[21:07:03] route-evaluator: p95_us_west_2=980ms -> trigger fallback to model-quantized-v1
[21:07:09] router: switched to us-east-1 (weight 0.6)
[21:07:35] route-evaluator: p95_us_east_1=340ms -> switch back to us-west-2
[21:08:00] repeated decision -> oscillation_count=3
```
Ophelia (product): Post-incident ask: add explicit model-quality score into routing decision so fallbacks consider quality delta not just latency. Put on roadmap.
Sanjay (infra): Quick note: the fallback model had lower memory pressure but worse decoding for our top domains; that tradeoff wasn't in the routing cost function.
Lucas (oncall): Monitoring: setting an alert to suppress identical reroute alerts for this thread to avoid noise.
Lucas (oncall): 21:45 UTC update: metrics stable. p95 ~285ms. Oscillation_count reset. CS informed. Creating follow-up ticket for SLO tuning + routing policy safeguards.
CS Ops (emma): fastchat-inc and neo-search ack customer notices received well. No escalations.
Maria (sre): Will own the postmortem writeup. Initial summary: rapid p95-based re-eval + aggressive rollout weights + low hysteresis => routing oscillation => temporary fallbacks to lower-quality model => customer impact. Action items: smoother eval window, min stable duration, oscillation detector, include model-quality into routing score, improve canarying + rollout playbook.
Ophelia (product): Thanks all. Please link PRs and postmortem to the ticket 1958123456. I'll coordinate prioritization with product and CS.
Lucas (oncall): Closing loop: if nobody sees recurrence in next 30m, I'll mark incident closed and update channel. :thumbsup:
Incident Bot: Incident 1958123456 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident assigned to Maria for postmortem and to Sanjay for routing hotfix.
